hypotheses.claim: The Qwen3.5 vision/mmproj representation can serve as the single deep visual backbone for Frank, feeding both MVC familiarity routing and semantic decode escalation, eliminating a duplicate heavy Retina encoder.
hypotheses.falsifier: A matched dedicated lightweight feature encoder materially dominates Qwen feature reuse on open-set/familiarity calibration or total task/resource Pareto performance.

hypotheses.claim: Raw generative Qwen vision representations will need a tiny learned projection/readout for stable user-specific familiarity/open-set geometry, but not a second heavy semantic vision encoder.
hypotheses.evidence: Qwen's own Qwen3-VL-Embedding family uses an explicit embedding/retrieval objective and dedicated embedding model path rather than claiming arbitrary base-VLM hidden states are already calibrated retrieval vectors.
hypotheses.falsifier: Raw pooled Qwen3.5 mmproj descriptors match or beat projected/dedicated embeddings on held-out familiar/near-neighbor unknown fixtures under equal total budget.

hypotheses.claim: Vision-encode-only plus MVC can safely bypass the 4B language decoder on a material fraction of recurring visual states.
hypotheses.falsifier: Decoder bypass rate is too low to save material cost, or bypass increases false familiarity/task failures beyond tolerance.

hypotheses.claim: Delta-guided ROI plus adaptive image-token budgets reduce visual-cycle cost while preserving GUI grounding and task success better than full-frame deep decode every cycle.
hypotheses.falsifier: ROI/context loss causes enough off-ROI modal, layout or small-text failures that matched full-frame processing is Pareto-superior.

hypotheses.claim: A hybrid of event/change processing plus periodic/on-demand full anchors is more robust than pure change-only visual sensing.
hypotheses.falsifier: Anchors add measurable resource cost without reducing stale-state, hidden-context or recovery failures.

hypotheses.claim: Action/outcome-linked visual crops plus compact typed state outperform repeated full-screenshot history for Frank's action verification and future retrieval under equal context budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Local memory repeatedly misses global context needed for correct later decisions and cannot be rescued cheaply by anchor retrieval.

hypotheses.claim: User-named visual entities can be learned more sample-efficiently by binding MVC visual prototypes to textual/name anchors in the same Qwen multimodal semantic space, while keeping sensor evidence separate from semantic labels.
hypotheses.origin: Interaction between Qwen native multimodality, Qwen3-VL unified multimodal embedding research, and Frank's GOLD user-label learning path.
hypotheses.falsifier: Text-anchor binding worsens instance-level discrimination/open-set calibration or causes semantic similarity to masquerade as visual identity.

hypotheses.claim: After a deterministic pixel/tile change gate, temporal distance in pooled Qwen visual features can estimate semantic-change magnitude and control whether full semantic decode is necessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Feature distance is unstable across benign crop/resolution/antialiasing changes or fails to separate semantically meaningful from irrelevant visual changes.

hypotheses.claim: Abliteration can leave low-level visual representation behavior mostly stable while still changing end-to-end visual decisions through the text/semantic decoder; therefore mmproj-level MVC compatibility and end-to-end visual action competence must be tested as separate layers.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched hashes/feature probes show the visual representation itself changes materially across the compared model export or the decoder change has no measurable visual-decision effect.
